title: Jubilant Yeasty Korean Persian Cucumber Kalguksu
description: A light and flaky Korean dish featuring Persian cucumber, this yeasty kalguksu is a perfect ovo-vegetarian friendly meal option. It is made with katsuramuki-cut cucumbers and a variety of spices.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, yeast, and salt, then gradually add warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough for about 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Let the dough rise in a warm place for about 1 hour, or until it has doubled in size.
Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces and roll each piece into a thin sheet.
Cut the sheets into kalguksu shapes, which are typically short and flat.
In a large pot, boil water and cook the kalguksu for about 5 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
In a pan, heat vegetable oil over medium heat and saute garlic and green onions until fragrant.
Add the cooked kalguksu to the pan and stir in soy sauce and sesame seeds.
In a small bowl, beat eggs and set aside.
Add the katsuramuki-cut cucumbers to the pan and stir-fry for about 2 minutes.
Pour the beaten eggs over the cucumbers and kalguksu, and stir-fry until the eggs are cooked through.
